raw_case_text:
A 41-year-old HIV-1-infected male farmer presented with a five-day history of right hypochondriac abdominal pain associated with decreased appetite, nausea, vomiting, and two days of yellowish discolouration of sclera, with no history of fever, diarrhoea, blurring of vision, and odynophagia or dysphagia.
He presented to us for the first time in September 2016, when he was diagnosed with pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonitis (PJP) on transbronchial lung biopsy and successfully treated with co-trimoxazole and prednisolone. This biopsy did not reveal CMV inclusion bodies. His CD4 count was 109/muL and HIV-1 viral load was 4.89 log copies/ml.
He was diagnosed with HIV-1 infection in 2000 and was treated by another physician, for which he was initiated on zidovudine (ZDV)/lamivudine (3TC)/nevirapine (NVP) and switched to tenofovir disproxil fumarate (TDF)/3TC/atazanavir/ritonavir (ATV/r) in 2011 due to virological failure. After control of PJP, we switched his HAART to raltegravir (RAL)/darunavir (DRV)/r based on the genotypic resistance report. Within 4 weeks of initiating HAART, he presented with the above mentioned symptoms.
Physical examination was unremarkable except for icterus and tender hepatomegaly. Fundoscopy did not reveal CMV retinitis. He had normocytic normochromic anaemia (Hb: 10.7 g/dl), normal total leucocyte, and differential counts. Liver enzymes were total bilirubin: 9.2 mg/dl (reference value: 0-1 mg/dl), aspartate transaminase (AST): 109 U/L [15-37 U/L], alanine transaminase (ALT): 41 U/L (14-59 U/L), and alkaline phosphatase (ALP): 906 U/L (46-116 U/L). Tests for hepatitis B and hepatitis C were negative.
Hepatomegaly (liver span-18 cm) with grade I-II intrahepatic biliary dilatation with focal parenchymal lesion was seen on abdominal ultrasound. The common bile duct (CBD) was dilated, measuring 14 mm suggestive of possible obstruction at the level of ampulla with no definitive mass or obstructive lesion.
An endoscopic retrograde cholangio-pancreatography (ERCP) was performed, which revealed oedematous papilla with stenosis. Cholangiogram showed a dilated CBD with prepapillary CBD stricture. All these features were suggestive of AIDS cholangiopathy (Figure 1(a)).
Wide papillotomy was performed, and a 7 Fr CBD stent was placed for biliary drainage. Bile aspirate was negative for Cryptosporidium, Microsporidium, Cyclospora, and Mycobacterium. Brush cytology of the stricture revealed inflammatory cells, pigment-laden macrophages, and several red blood cells with no acid-fast organisms.
Histopathological examination of ampullary biopsy showed focal ulcerations with superficial mucosal necrosis and acute and chronic inflammation in the mucosa and lamina propria. Cells of submucosal Brunner's glands showed nucleomegaly with eosinophilic intranuclear and basophilic cytoplasmic CMV inclusions (Figure 1(b)).
After intervention, the patient had immediate symptomatic relief and did not receive any anti-CMV treatment. Liver enzymes normalised 2 weeks later.
After 6 months, CD4 improved to 363 cells/muL with HIV viral load of 423 copies/ml. Repeat ERCP revealed normal cholangiogram with no residual stricture in lower CBD, with normal papilla (Figure 2(a)). Previously placed stent had migrated out. Cells from ampullary biopsies did not reveal intranuclear/cytoplasmic CMV inclusions (Figure 2(b)).
A repeat viral load after 8 months was <50 copies/ml. ART was switched to dolutegravir (DTG)/DRV/r.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 41-year-old HIV-1-infected male farmer presented with a 5-day history of right hypochondriac abdominal pain, anorexia, nausea, and vomiting, and 2 days of scleral icterus.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Diagnosed with HIV-1 in 2000 (previously treated with ZDV/3TC/NVP and switched in 2011 to TDF/3TC/ATV/r for virological failure), the patient had presented in September 2016 with biopsy-proven Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (CD4 109/uL, HIV-1 viral load 4.89 log copies/mL; lung biopsy negative for CMV inclusions), which was treated with co-trimoxazole and prednisolone followed by resistance-guided HAART switch to raltegravir plus darunavir/ritonavir (RAL/DRV/r). Within 4 weeks of starting RAL/DRV/r, he developed 5 days of right upper quadrant abdominal pain, anorexia, nausea, and vomiting, and 2 days of scleral jaundice.
subjective.past_medical_history: HIV-1 infection (diagnosed in 2000) status post recent Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (September 2016). Occupation: farmer.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for 5 days of right hypochondriac pain, anorexia, nausea, vomiting, and 2 days of jaundice. Pertinent negatives: no fever, diarrhea, visual blurring, odynophagia, or dysphagia. Home medications: raltegravir, darunavir/ritonavir, and co-trimoxazole.

objective.physical_examination: Scleral icterus and tender hepatomegaly (liver span 18 cm); fundoscopic examination showed no CMV retinitis; remainder of physical exam unremarkable.
objective.routine_investigations: Normocytic normochromic anemia (hemoglobin 10.7 g/dL), normal WBC and differential counts, total bilirubin 9.2 mg/dL (ref 0-1 mg/dL), AST 109 U/L (ref 15-37 U/L), ALT 41 U/L (ref 14-59 U/L), and markedly elevated alkaline phosphatase (ALP) 906 U/L (ref 46-116 U/L); hepatitis B and C tests negative. Abdominal ultrasound showed hepatomegaly (18 cm), grade I-II intrahepatic biliary dilatation, a focal parenchymal lesion, and a dilated common bile duct (CBD, 14 mm) to the level of the ampulla without a discrete mass.
objective.advanced_workup: Baseline CD4 count was 109 cells/uL and HIV-1 viral load was 4.89 log copies/mL (improving at 6 months to CD4 363 cells/uL and HIV viral load 423 copies/mL, and <50 copies/mL at 8 months). Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) demonstrated an edematous, stenotic major papilla and a 14-mm dilated CBD with a prepapillary distal CBD stricture consistent with AIDS cholangiopathy (wide endoscopic papillotomy and 7 Fr CBD stent placement performed). Bile aspirate and stricture brush cytology were negative for Cryptosporidium, Microsporidia, Cyclospora, and acid-fast mycobacteria. Ampullary mucosal biopsy revealed focal ulceration, superficial mucosal necrosis, mixed inflammation, and submucosal Brunner's gland cells exhibiting nucleomegaly with characteristic eosinophilic intranuclear and basophilic cytoplasmic cytomegalovirus (CMV) inclusions.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Definitive diagnosis of cytomegalovirus (CMV)-associated AIDS cholangiopathy (papillary stenosis and prepapillary CBD stricture) unmasked as immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS) 4 weeks after starting raltegravir/darunavir/ritonavir, confirmed by characteristic eosinophilic intranuclear and basophilic cytoplasmic CMV inclusions in submucosal Brunner's glands on ampullary biopsy (with Cryptosporidium, Microsporidia, Cyclospora, and mycobacteria excluded). Treated with ERCP wide endoscopic papillotomy, 7 Fr biliary stenting, and continued HAART without systemic anti-CMV therapy, resulting in immediate symptom relief, normalization of liver enzymes within 2 weeks, and complete resolution of the CBD stricture and histological disappearance of CMV inclusions on 6-month repeat ERCP and ampullary biopsy.
